previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a complex history of sclerosing mesenteritis, chronic abdominal pain, TPN dependence via femoral catheter, and recurrent line infections was admitted for fever, chills, and erythema at her left femoral line site with purulent discharge. She was started on IV vancomycin for suspected catheter-related infection. Blood cultures were negative, and a chest X-ray showed no pneumonia. Due to contraindication from a spinal stimulator, an MRV was not performed. The infected left femoral catheter was removed and replaced with a new tunneled line in the right femoral vein. The catheter tip culture later showed no growth. TPN was held during admission and will be resumed at home. Antibiotics were discontinued at discharge. She remained afebrile, with stable labs and controlled symptoms. She was discharged home with instructions to monitor the new line site and resume her prior medication and TPN regimen.

Summary:  ___ with complex medical/surgical history admitted 
from the ED for subacute on chronic worsening of abdominal pain

protocol of 0.25mg IV dilaudid q15minutes up to maximum of 1mg 
over 1 hour for pain management, and is typically discharge 
home.  On this day, the patient was admitted.  Surgery felt 
there was no intervention indicated.  CT scan showed chronic 
partial SBO, possibly with slight interval worsening. After 24 
hours, the patient was given a trial of pain protocol, PO 
phenergan, and a trial of PO liquids/food.  The patient 
tolerated this exceptionally, and was discharged home. She will 
folow-up with ___ on ___ regarding changing her G tube (for

.

home, this med is non-formulary and she uses her home meds while 
admitted, when available.  She did not have them this admission, 
and when the pt developed a headache she responded very well to 
Fioricet, 1 tab.

# GI dysmotility:  home rabeprazole, octreotide, misoprostol 
continued.

tolerated POs before discharge
